To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the design of living sensing systems can support community engagement with urban environments, (2) these designs must support the appropriation of the living sensing system by the community, and (3) the community can appropriate a living sensing system by making it their own, and by making it work for them.

living sensing systems can be designed to support collective engagements, which can be characterized as a shift from the individual to the collective, from the instant to the long term, and from the digital to the material.
living sensing systems offer a new perspective on materiality, time and collective modes of participation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how living sensing systems can engage communities in new forms of participation, and how they might be designed and deployed to support these engagements.
the development of living sensing systems that support new ways of knowing and engaging with living systems.
the design of living sensing systems, and the role that these systems play in the everyday practices of community engagement.

this project provides a new perspective on how we might engage with living sensing systems in HCI.
the work presented here provides a foundation for future work on living sensing systems, which can help to inform the development of new technologies for environmental monitoring.
this work is a contribution to the HCI community, as it explores new design spaces that are enabled by the intersection of organic and digital materials, and the implications for HCI design.

we have developed a new approach for engaging the public in understanding how bacteria can be used to remediate soil.
we are interested in the design and deployment, and the study and evaluation of living sensing systems that support community engagements with environmental sensing.

living sensing systems offer opportunities for new kinds of engagements with the natural world.
